choices.text: Increase the staging table's partition expiration so the stale rows disappear without any explicit delete
Run the delete first and the insert second, so that a failure leaves rows in neither table until the next night
Wrap the insert and the delete in one multi-statement transaction that commits both changes together or rolls both back
Add a second scheduled query to remove duplicates in the history table after the nightly job has finished

stem: A batch pipeline appends each day's extract to a BigQuery table with a plain insert. When the orchestrator retries a task after a timeout, the same day's rows are appended twice. The team wants any retry or rerun to leave the table in the same final state. Which change achieves that?

Add a column with the load time, so that duplicate rows can be told apart by timestamp when anyone queries them later
Disable retries in the orchestrator so that a timeout can never lead to a second run of the task

stem: A ride-hailing app stores each rider's recent trip state in Bigtable with replication across two regions. After a rider updates a pickup point, the app immediately reads it back and sometimes shows the older value. Availability during a regional outage still matters. What is the best design?

choices.text: Add a Memorystore cache in front of both clusters and treat it as the source of truth for pickup points
Route the app through an app profile with single-cluster routing and fail over to the other cluster only when needed
Use multi-cluster routing for all traffic, because it always returns the latest write in any cluster
Disable replication and keep a single cluster in one region, since replication is the only reason data is eventually consistent

stem: A media analytics company writes its batch and streaming transformations today on Dataflow. Convert the pipelines into Cloud Data Fusion visual graphs and export the graph definitions as JSON files
Build the transformations as BigQuery stored procedures and call them from scheduled queries on a fixed timetable

stem: A retailer's clickstream data sits in Amazon S3 buckets in an AWS region. Its contract requires that the raw files must not leave that region. Schedule a nightly Storage Transfer Service job that copies the S3 objects into a Cloud Storage bucket
Create BigLake tables over the S3 data using BigQuery Omni, and join them with BigQuery tables
Use Datastream to replicate the S3 objects as change events into a BigQuery dataset each hour

stem: A data science group runs Apache Spark on its own clusters, while the BI team uses BigQuery. External tables over CSV files, which BigQuery reads while Spark keeps its own working copy
Native BigQuery storage tables, which Spark reads through a nightly export into Parquet files
Apache Iceberg managed tables, with data in your buckets and Iceberg metadata open engines can read

stem: A team wants to analyse clickstream objects that stay in Amazon S3 by using BigQuery Omni. Which TWO statements about this design are correct? (Select TWO)

A query run from a BigQuery region can join the Omni table with local BigQuery tables, filtering remote data first

The team first creates a connection to Amazon S3, then a BigLake table that references the bucket

stem: A bank is designing a new analytics platform and wants to limit lock-in without giving up managed services. Which TWO design decisions best support portability of its data and processing? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Store curated datasets in open file formats such as Parquet or Avro in Cloud Storage with schemas documented
Use cloud-specific serialisation formats for messages so that consumers must use the same client libraries
Place every dataset only in the warehouse's proprietary native storage and expose it through its SQL dialect alone
Encode business rules inside the configuration screens of a single orchestration product rather than in code
Implement transformations with the Apache Beam SDK so the pipeline code is not tied to one runner

stem: A logistics company ingests partner shipment files, cleans them, and loads curated tables into BigQuery. The cleaning rules change several times a year, and auditors sometimes ask to re-derive a table as it was a year ago. Which staging design best meets these needs?

choices.text: Load files straight into the final BigQuery tables and use table snapshots as the only record of history
Apply cleaning in the ingestion step and keep only cleaned rows so that storage use stays small
Keep raw files on the partners' servers and re-request them whenever the rules change
Land every incoming file unchanged in a Cloud Storage raw zone, then build curated tables from it

stem: A ticketing company needs a dashboard that shows sales within a few seconds of each purchase. Traffic is mostly quiet but jumps by orders of magnitude when popular events go on sale. Write purchases to a Cloud SQL instance and refresh a spreadsheet extract at the top of each hour
Publish purchase events to Pub/Sub, process them with a Dataflow streaming pipeline, and write to BigQuery
Collect events in a Dataproc cluster sized for the peak and run a Spark batch job every few minutes

stem: A company has about 200 existing Spark jobs on an on-premises Hadoop cluster. The jobs use custom JARs and Spark libraries and run nightly. Dataproc, which runs Spark and Hadoop jobs largely unchanged on managed clusters
BigQuery, after translating every job into scheduled SQL queries
Cloud Data Fusion, after rebuilding each job as a visual pipeline from scratch

stem: A company is moving a Hadoop cluster to Google Cloud. Its HDFS holds 300 TB that is mostly cold between monthly jobs, and the team wants to stop paying for always-on disks and to run Spark on temporary clusters. Which design decouples storage from compute?

Rebuild an HDFS cluster on persistent disks in the cloud and keep it running between monthly jobs
Load the data into a Memorystore instance shared by all clusters and read it over the network
Keep the data in Cloud Storage and read it from Spark and Hadoop jobs through the Cloud Storage connector

stem: A team lands event data from many producers into Cloud Storage for later loading to BigQuery and Spark. Producers' schemas gain new optional fields every few months. Which file format best fits the landing zone?

stem: A company runs a 2 TB MySQL database on premises that backs an order system. It wants to move to Cloud SQL for MySQL and can tolerate only a few minutes of downtime at cutover. Which approach fits?

BigQuery Data Transfer Service scheduled MySQL transfers into a BigQuery dataset, then export to Cloud SQL
Database Migration Service continuous migration: initial load, ongoing replication, then promotion
Datastream to Cloud Storage, followed by a manual import of the files into Cloud SQL after hours

stem: An insurer wants its Oracle operational database on premises to stay in place, but analysts need the data in BigQuery within seconds of each change, without adding noticeable load to the source. Which service fits this requirement?

stem: A compliance team wants a BigQuery table that records every insert, update and delete made to a PostgreSQL table on premises, so that it can reconstruct the state of a row at any past moment. stem: A school district must move a 40 GB PostgreSQL database to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL. The system is used only during school hours, and the district accepts a full weekend of downtime. Datastream replication to BigQuery, then export the tables into Cloud SQL

stem: A manufacturer wants to copy 600 TB of files from an on-premises NAS to Cloud Storage and then keep new and changed files synchronised every night. stem: A logistics company runs Apache Kafka in its own data center. Events must land in BigQuery for reporting, the team wants to avoid writing and operating a custom consumer, and the data center is linked to the VPC network by Cloud Interconnect. Which approach fits?

stem: An analytics team stores 5 million support tickets in a BigQuery table. They want to label each ticket with a sentiment and a short list of topics, keep the results in a new table, and avoid exporting data or building a custom ML model. What is the most direct approach?

stem: A claims team keeps 200,000 scanned PDF claim forms in a Cloud Storage bucket. They need fields such as claimant name, claim date and amount extracted into typed BigQuery columns, with the work done from SQL. Which design fits?

stem: A finance analyst needs one SQL statement, a MERGE into a reporting table, to run every night at 02:00. Nothing depends on it and no other tasks need coordination. Which option is the best fit?

stem: A DAG in Cloud Composer waits for a partner file to arrive in Cloud Storage, which may take from minutes to many hours. During busy mornings, many waiting tasks have used up all the worker slots and other DAGs are delayed. What is the best fix?

stem: A team develops Cloud Composer DAGs in a Git repository. They want changes to be validated automatically before production and want the production environment to pick up only reviewed code. Which TWO practices fit? (Select TWO)

stem: Partner files arrive in a Cloud Storage bucket at unpredictable times, and each arrival must start a Cloud Composer DAG run immediately with the file name as input. What is the recommended design?

stem: A workflow calls an external inventory API through an HTTP step. The API occasionally returns HTTP 503 for a few seconds, and the workflow then fails and needs a manual restart. Which change makes the workflow resilient with the least code?

stem: A workflow must start a BigQuery query job, wait until it completes, and then continue. The author does not want to write polling loops or manage job IDs by hand. What should the workflow use?

stem: Which TWO situations favor Cloud Composer over Workflows for orchestration? (Select TWO)

stem: A Cloud Composer DAG needs a database password and an API key. Developers currently store them as Airflow variables in the DAG code repository. The security team wants the secrets out of source control and centrally rotated. What should the data engineer do?

stem: A Cloud Composer DAG creates a Dataproc cluster, runs a Spark job and then deletes the cluster. When the Spark job fails, the delete task is skipped as an upstream failure, and the cluster keeps running and billing until someone notices. What change fixes this?

stem: Which TWO workloads are the best fit for Bigtable? (Select TWO)

stem: A global payments company is building a ledger that must stay strongly consistent across three continents, support SQL and multi-row transactions, scale beyond a single machine, and keep serving through a regional outage with no manual failover. stem: An operations team runs a PostgreSQL application that records orders. Managers also run heavy aggregate reports on the live data throughout the day, which today slows order entry. stem: A regional HR department runs a MySQL application with 200 GB of data, a few hundred concurrent users and no plans for global growth. The team wants managed backups, a standby in another zone, and no application changes. Which choice is the most cost-effective fit?

Bigtable with a row key made from the primary key, because it is cheaper than relational databases at every size

stem: A startup is building a mobile and web app whose users create nested documents such as notes with comments. The app needs real-time updates pushed to clients, offline use on phones with later sync, automatic scaling and no server to manage. Which database fits?

stem: A gaming company keeps player profiles in a relational database. A live leaderboard and session lookups are read tens of thousands of times per second and must respond in under a millisecond. Data can be rebuilt from the database if lost. What should the data engineer add?

stem: Every night a data engineer must call a partner REST API, wait for a Cloud Run job to finish, run one BigQuery load and then post a status message. The steps are strictly sequential, need no Python code, and the team wants no environment to size or patch. Which scheduling design fits best?

A Cloud Composer environment with a DAG for the four steps, kept running around the clock for this one job
Cloud Scheduler triggering a Workflows workflow that calls each service in order and waits for the result

stem: A BigQuery scheduled query appends the previous hour's aggregates to a reporting table with INSERT. It is set to run at exactly the top of every hour. Occasionally the same hour's rows appear twice. What should the data engineer do?

Change the query to run as a batch priority job so BigQuery guarantees it executes exactly one time
Move the schedule off the exact hour, such as a few minutes past, and make the statement safe to repeat
Replace the schedule with a Cloud Monitoring alert that reruns the query whenever a duplicate is detected

stem: A Cloud Composer DAG loads one day of sales into BigQuery with an append task. Operations often re-run failed days from the Airflow UI, and finance has found doubled revenue on re-run days. The engineer wants the DAG to be safe to re-run for any date. Which change achieves that?

Put the whole extract, transform and load code in a single PythonOperator task so only one task can fail

stem: A team's Cloud Composer DAGs set `email_on_failure` to True, yet nobody has ever received a failure email, and the team also wants to hear at once if the whole environment stops being healthy, not just a single task. Which TWO actions address this? (Select TWO)

stem: After a team added forty new DAGs, Cloud Composer tasks start late and the scheduler seems busy even when few tasks run. The new DAG files query BigQuery and read a configuration table at the top of the file, outside any task. What is the most likely cause and fix?

stem: A media analytics team runs BigQuery on the on-demand model. Monthly cost swings widely because of occasional very large queries, and finance wants predictable spend with some headroom for peaks. Utilisation is fairly steady during working hours. What should the data engineer propose?

Create one reservation per analyst project with no baseline and no autoscaling to share costs evenly
Stay on on-demand and ask users to run every query as a batch job so bytes processed stay constant
Buy a very large fixed baseline sized for the worst peak ever seen and leave autoscaling switched off

stem: A team created a Standard edition reservation, assigned a project to it and later decided the workload needs another edition's capabilities. They try to change the edition on the existing reservation and cannot. What does the documentation say they must do?

Edit the capacity commitment, because the commitment alone decides the edition of its reservations

stem: Finance questions a bill. A reservation autoscales, and the data engineer compares the autoscaled slots billed for a day with the slot usage summed from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS. The billed number is clearly higher. Which explanation is correct?

stem: A nightly financial close runs in a reservation that has no baseline and no autoscaling and relies on idle slots borrowed from other reservations. When other teams are busy the close misses its deadline. Which TWO changes make the close dependable? (Select TWO)

Run the close as a batch priority job, because batch jobs are protected from slot preemption

BigQuery splits the project's jobs across all reservations in the region until the assignment completes

stem: In a reservation shared by dashboards and nightly data-quality scans, the scans are not time critical but sometimes slow dashboard queries when all slots are busy. What should the data engineer do for the scans?

stem: The owner of a source table plans to drop a column. The platform team needs to know which downstream BigQuery tables and reports depend on it, several levels deep, before approving the change. What helps most?

choices.text: Search the catalog for the column name and assume the tables returned are the only dependents
Check the table's data profile statistics for the column to see if it is used by other tables
Use the catalog's data lineage graph and a downstream impact analysis from the table
Review the BI Engine reservation statistics to see which dashboards read the column

stem: Consumers of a published data product keep emailing the producing team to ask for access and for the refresh schedule. The producers want consumers to self-serve both. Which TWO data product capabilities address this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A contract that states agreed terms, such as the refresh schedule and quality expectations, which consumers can read
A policy tag on every table that makes the data product public to all principals in the organization
A lineage graph that lists the owner's email addresses so that consumers can contact the team directly
A BI Engine reservation that caches the data product tables so that consumers can read them without permissions
Access groups that map roles such as Reader and Analyst to Google Groups, so consumers request the appropriate level of access

stem: A Looker dashboard queries a 2 TB fact table joined with a few small dimension tables, filtering on the last 30 days. Queries take several seconds, and 200 users refresh at the start of the working day. The team wants sub-second response without changing the BI tool. What should they do?

choices.text: Export the fact table to Cloud Storage as CSV files and point the dashboard at those files
Reserve BI Engine capacity in the table's region and set the fact and dimension tables as preferred tables
Move the dimension tables to Cloud SQL so that the joins execute in a relational database
Convert the fact table to an external table so that every dashboard query runs against Cloud Storage objects

stem: A team reserved BI Engine capacity, but dashboards that query a BigLake table over Parquet files in Cloud Storage see no acceleration. They need responsive dashboards on this data and can tolerate hourly freshness. What should they do?

choices.text: Schedule a query that writes the results to a native BigQuery table every hour and point the dashboards at that table
Increase the BI Engine reservation size, because BigLake tables are accelerated once enough memory exists
Create a logical view over the BigLake table and add the view to the preferred tables list
Disable the query cache so that BI Engine is forced to accelerate every request

stem: A large events table receives inserts all day, and a dashboard repeatedly runs the same aggregation grouped by country and day. Users must always see current numbers, and the team wants the lowest compute cost for repeated queries. Which design fits?

choices.text: A BI Engine reservation alone, because it recomputes aggregates over all rows less expensively than caching
A standard logical view over the events table, because views store the computed results of the aggregation
An incremental materialized view of the aggregation, which combines its cached results with new base table data at query time
A scheduled query that rebuilds a summary table every six hours and a dashboard that reads that table

stem: A materialized view over a sales table was fast for weeks. After the source team started running UPDATE and DELETE statements that rewrite historical rows in the base table, queries on the view became slow and expensive until the next refresh. Why?

choices.text: Smart tuning permanently disables any materialized view when its base table receives DML statements
Materialized views are removed automatically when any base table row is changed, so queries read the base table directly until it is recreated
BI Engine invalidates the view each time historical rows change, and the reservation must be recreated before the view is used again
Updates or deletions to base table data stop incremental updates, so BigQuery cannot use the view's cached data until the view is refreshed

stem: A product has several dashboards that all group the same 5 billion row table by region and month, and developers write queries against the base table in many places. The team wants those queries to get faster without changing any query text. Which feature does this?

choices.text: A BI Engine preferred-table list, because it rewrites queries to read precomputed aggregates
A clustered base table, because clustering stores aggregated results for each cluster key
A scheduled query that writes a summary table, because BigQuery redirects matching base-table queries to it
A materialized view, because smart tuning can rewrite base table queries to use its results

stem: An analytics engineer calculates customer lifetime value, return rate and 90-day churn flag in every dashboard query with long CASE and window logic over raw order lines. Dashboards are slow and the formulas drift between reports. How should the engineer prepare the data?

choices.text: Precalculate the fields in a Dataform model into a curated reporting table that all dashboards read
Keep the logic inside each dashboard so that every report owner can adjust the formula to local needs and refresh timing
Export the raw order lines to a spreadsheet and calculate the fields there for each report
Normalize the order lines into more tables so that each field is a join away from its inputs

stem: In the execution details of a slow BigQuery query, a join stage outputs far more rows than it receives as input, and the later stages spend most of their time on those rows. What is the most effective change?

choices.text: Add more BI Engine memory, because join row explosion is caused by a shortage of cache
Convert the query to SELECT * so that BigQuery can choose the best columns to scan itself
Filter or pre-aggregate the inputs before the join, and check that the join keys match the intended relationship
Raise the LIMIT value of the query so that each slot processes more rows at a time and the stage finishes sooner

stem: An hourly BigQuery report normally takes 40 seconds under on-demand pricing. Today it takes several minutes. The query plan timeline shows the number of active units staying low while the amount of queued units of work stays high, and nothing in the query text changed. What does this point to, and what should be done?

choices.text: A BI Engine cache miss, so the reservation size should be increased until the miss rate is zero
Slot contention with other queries, so reduce concurrent load or move the workload to reserved capacity
A partitioning mistake in the table, so the table should be recreated with clustering on all columns
A data skew in the first stage only, so the query should add ORDER BY to even out the work

stem: A data engineer opens BigQuery's query performance insights for a slow query. Which TWO kinds of findings can the insights report? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Missing indexes, which the engineer must create on the join columns
Cluster imbalance across Compute Engine nodes in the query's worker pool
Stale statistics, which the engineer must refresh by running ANALYZE on the table
Slot contention, where the query waited because slots were limited
Partition skew, where an oversized join partition could not be rebalanced

stem: Analysts must query a customers table in BigQuery. Compliance says the national ID column must be visible only to the fraud team, and analysts should still be able to run SELECT * queries on the table. Which design satisfies both?

choices.text: Tag the national ID column with a policy tag and give analysts no further access, so that their SELECT * queries run on the remaining columns
Tag the national ID column with a policy tag, grant the fraud team Fine-Grained Reader, and give analysts masked access through a data policy
Create a logical view without the national ID column and give analysts access to both the view and the base table
Move the national ID column to a separate Cloud Storage bucket and ask the fraud team to join the data by hand

stem: Analysts must join the orders table to a customer table on the email column to count repeat buyers, but must not see actual addresses. Joins must still work across both tables. Which masking rule should the data engineer apply for analysts?

choices.text: Nullify, which returns NULL and hides the value so that the join still finds matching rows
Default masking value, which returns the same constant for every email so that rows still match uniquely
Hash (SHA-256), which returns a type-preserving hash so equal values stay equal and can be joined
Last four characters, which returns the last four characters so that matching is still unique

stem: A team using column-level security finds that analysts' existing queries break with an error whenever the queries read a protected column through SELECT *. They want existing queries to keep working while the raw values stay hidden. What change achieves this?

choices.text: Attach a data policy with a masking rule to the policy tag and grant analysts the Masked Reader role, so queries return masked values
Grant analysts the Fine-Grained Reader role on the tag so that errors stop and values stay protected
Drop the policy tag from the column and rely on dataset-level roles to hide the values
Rewrite each existing query to list all columns except the protected ones, as column-level control requires

stem: A company does not know which of its BigQuery tables contain personal data across 300 projects. It wants continuous discovery that classifies columns and reports data sensitivity and risk levels, and later wants to share transformed data without identifying values. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Use BI Engine to scan columns for patterns and apply bucketing through reservations
Use Sensitive Data Protection discovery to profile data, then tokenization where needed
Train a BigQuery ML classifier on column names and use its output as the compliance record
Create policy tags manually on every column of the 300 projects before any inspection happens, then review them yearly

stem: Data analysts who know SQL but not Python want to predict customer churn from 80 million rows in BigQuery. They want to avoid moving data out of the warehouse and need categorical columns and numeric columns prepared as part of the model. What fits best?

choices.text: BigQuery ML logistic regression using automatic preprocessing or the TRANSFORM clause for features
Use BI Engine to learn churn patterns from the table in memory and read scores in dashboards
Build a Dataproc cluster to run Spark MLlib after copying the table into HDFS
Export the table to CSV files and train a custom model on a Compute Engine VM with GPUs

stem: A churn model built in BigQuery ML scored well in evaluation, but its predictions are poor in production, where requests arrive as raw rows. The training query computed scaled and bucketed features in a separate SELECT that is not reused at prediction time. What is the most robust fix?

choices.text: Disable automatic preprocessing and rely on prediction callers to scale values correctly
Retrain with more rows from the same table and keep the preprocessing in a separate query
Create a materialized view with the bucketing logic and ask callers to read from it per prediction request, while the model keeps its own features
Move the feature logic into the TRANSFORM clause of CREATE MODEL, so the same preprocessing is applied at evaluation and prediction

stem: A team forecasts demand from three years of weekly data with a BigQuery ML regression model. One feature is the average discount of the week being predicted, and rows were split randomly into training and evaluation sets. Evaluation accuracy is very high, but real accuracy is low. Which TWO data preparation problems explain this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Weekly granularity, because BigQuery ML models cannot train on data that has been aggregated by period
Too few distinct columns, because BigQuery ML cannot compute feature statistics unless many columns exist
Data leakage, because a feature uses information from the period being predicted that is unavailable at prediction time
Automatic preprocessing, because it always standardizes numeric inputs in a way that inflates evaluation scores
A random split of time-ordered rows, because evaluation rows then mix in periods that lie close to or before training rows

stem: A data engineer reviews which dashboard queries BI Engine can accelerate in a project. Which TWO queries will NOT be accelerated? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A query over a pre-aggregated native table that returns a few thousand rows
A query that calls a JavaScript user-defined function on each row of a native table
A large native fact table joined to a few small dimension tables, filtered by date
A grouped aggregation over a native partitioned table with a small number of joins
A query over a BigLake table whose data sits as Parquet files in Cloud Storage
